3631.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pnew- (“to breathe, sneeze”). Cognates include Old English fnēosan (English sneeze).

3644.t: From Proto-Hellenic *putʰmḗn, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰudʰmḗn. Cognate with πύνδαξ (púndax), Sanskrit बुध्न (budhná), Latin fundus, Old Armenian անդունդ (andund), Old English botm (English bottom).

3692.t: Found in late Greek, of uncertain origin, but possibly related to μαυρός (maurós, “dark”) (but see that entry and Μαῦρος (Maûros) for more theories about that word's origins).

3645.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

3669.t: Uncertain. The sense “penis” likely developed from a more concrete sense, and has been compared to βαλλία (ballĭ́ā, “private parts”) and the ethnonym Τριβαλλοί (Trĭbălloí).

3615.t: From πάροιμος (pároimos, “by the road, neighbor”) + -ία (-ía), or from παρα- (para-, “next, near, alongside, nearby, nigh”) + οἴμη (oímē, “song, tale”) + -ία (-ía, feminine suffix of abstraction).

3661.t: Unknown. Traditionally believed to be a substantivization of the adjective σχέδιος (skhédios, “near, close”).

3662.t: From τέλος (télos, “aim, purpose”) + -τή (-tḗ), probably formed by analogy with γενετή (genetḗ, “the hour of birth”) from γένος (génos, “kin”).

3690.t: From Proto-Hellenic *akmā́, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“point, sharp”). Cognates include ἀκή (akḗ, “point”) and ἄκρος (ákros).

3678.t: According to Beekes, a Pre-Greek origin is probable, as it is difficult to explain "χαλ-" from Indo-European and as a suffix "-ιν-" is frequent in Pre-Greek.

3643.t: From πτερόω (pteróō, “to feather”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

3629.t: Back-formation from πλανάω (planáō, “to wander, to roam”).

3601.t: Uncertain. Traditionally connected to μέλλω (méllō, “to intend, to mean to”), but Beekes considers this semantically weak.

3687.t: A reduplicative nominal formation, likely Attic, of the root of ἄγω (ágō, “to lead”).

3675.t: From φρύγω (phrū́gō, “to roast”) + -ανον (-anon), as dry firewood was traditionally used to start fires and roast food.

3685.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- (“corner, hirn”), the same source as ἄγκος (ắnkos, “glen; dell”), ἄγκυρα (ắnkūră, “anchor”) and ἀγκύλος (ănkŭ́los, “curved; bent”).

3680.t: Related to χνόη (khnóē, “axle-box”). Both words have been connected to χναύω (khnaúō, “to nibble”) and χνίω (khníō, “to break in small pieces”).

3660.t: Julius Pokorny connects this word with σπαίρω (spaírō, “to hammer, to make rapid movements”).

3652.t: From Hebrew שִׁקְמָה (shikmá, “sycamore”), with assimilation to σῦκον (sûkon, “fig”).

3613.t: From παρα- (para-, “beside, by”) + τείνω (teínō, “to stretch out”).

3650.t: From Proto-Hellenic *sténō, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tenh₂- (“to thunder”), compare Sanskrit स्तनति (stanati, “to drone, thunder”), Proto-Germanic *stenaną (“to moan, groan”), Proto-Slavic *stenàti (“to groan, to moan”).

3624.t: περι- (perĭ-, “around, about”) + στόμιον (stómĭon, “small mouth, mouth of a vessel, any aperture or opening, ornament for the neck”) + -ος (-os, adjective ending)

3677.t: Uncertain, with Beekes suggesting Pre-Greek origin based on the opaque phonology and semantic domain. May be related to φορύνω (phorū́nō, “to be mingled”) and/or πορφύρω (porphū́rō, “to heave, surge up”).

3639.t: From προσ- (pros-, “to, toward”) + τρέχω (trékhō, “to run, run over”).

3634.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ph₃tós (“(having been) drunk”). Cognate with Latin pōtus and Sanskrit पी॒त (pītá).

3664.t: From τόξον (tóxon) + -εύω (-eúō), possibly from Iranian. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀵𐀒𐀰𐀲 (to-ko-so-ta) (archer).
